sections.h2: When does the Alpena County recording desk take your deed?
sections.html:
The register works out of 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, and answers at 989-354-9547. According to the county office page, hours run 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

Recording cutoffs come sooner than closing time. An e-filing must land by 3:30 p.m. to count that day, and paper has until 4:00 p.m. at the window. Anything later joins the next business day's pile, so a Friday 4:15 delivery waits for Monday.

The register insists on originals. Once indexed, the original is returned to the sender, normally inside seven days of recording. No blank deeds are given out, and staff cannot coach you through completing one; the page sends people to an office supply store, a lawyer or a title company.

sections.h2: Which fees does Alpena County collect for recording and copies?
sections.html:
Most Michigan counties follow MCL 600.2567, which prices a recording at one flat sum no matter the number of pages. A charter county can override that by ordinance, so phone the register for the exact total before a check goes in the mail.

  • $30 for every recorded paper, and $3 more for each extra instrument it assigns or discharges.
  • Copies at $1 per page and certification at $5.
  • Index searches at 50 cents a year for grantor and grantee names, never less than $5.
  • A tax certification fee on certain deeds. Ask the Alpena County treasurer whether yours qualifies.

Links on the office page lead to a fee sheet, a recording requirements sheet and e-recording instructions.

sections.h2: What search and alert tools does the Alpena County register run?
sections.html:
Researchers can choose Laredo or Tapestry. Per the county, Tapestry fits someone who needs a copy or two, and Laredo suits title companies and frequent searchers.

Two free services cover Alpena County only: a property fraud alert and a notary fraud alert. Each sends a call, text or email when a recorded paper carries your name.

The same office is a certified passport agent and takes passport photos,, so some visitors are there for a passport.

sections.h2: What will state and county transfer tax cost on an Alpena County house?
sections.html:
A typical Alpena County house, valued at $153,900 in the 2020 to 2024 Census estimate, holds 308 units of $500. On each unit the seller pays 55 cents to the county (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 to the state (MCL 207.525).

Transfer tax on a $153,900 Alpena County sale (308 units of $500), worked from MCL 207.504 and 207.525
PartMathResult
County308 x $0.55$169.40
State308 x $3.75$1,155.00
Both308 x $4.30$1,324.40

Remit it to the Alpena County treasurer inside 15 days after delivery. When furniture or equipment rides along, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an attached affidavit lists the values separately.

sections.h2: Which distress and court transfers escape the Alpena County transfer tax?
sections.html:
Distressed owners and heirs should read MCL 207.526, because several exemptions fit their situations.

  • A deed handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it. The lender's own resale is still taxed.
  • A court of record's order moving title, when no price is set.
  • An installment land contract, while legal title sits with the seller.
  • Husband and wife moving property into or out of a tenancy by the entireties.

Paid in error? Treasury takes refund requests.

sections.h2: What details on a deed trip up an Alpena County recording?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording act, MCL 565.201, lets a register refuse a paper that skips basic identification steps. Returns usually trace to one of these:

  • A signer's printed name that differs from the name in the notary's certificate.
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue.
  • No notary name printed next to the notary's signature.
  • No street address for the buyer, or no drafter name and address.
  • A full Social Security number left visible.
  • Foreign-language text without an English version attached.

Once a paper satisfies the act, the register has no right to refuse it over what it says.

sections.h2: How should you time a deed against the Alpena County cutoffs?
sections.html:
Start the e-record by early afternoon, because the 3:30 p.m. cutoff arrives half an hour before the counter's 4:00. Before signing, run through a short list:

  • The buyer's mailing address appears on the deed.
  • The notary's name is printed beside the signature.
  • The full sale value is stated, or a value affidavit is attached.
  • The original, not a copy, goes to the register.
  • Any tax certification step has been cleared with the county treasurer.

Miss the cutoff and your record date moves to the next business day.

sections.h2: What is Alpena County like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
In the northeast of Michigan's Lower Peninsula, Alpena County fronts Lake Huron and Thunder Bay, and the Thunder Bay River drains most of its land. Lawmakers drew the county in 1840 as Anamickee, changed the name in 1843, and set up local government in 1857. The 45th parallel cuts across the county, and Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary lies offshore, with automated lighthouses on Middle Island and Thunder Bay Island.

Alpena is the county seat and its only city. Hillman is a village that straddles the county line, and Alpena Charter Township and the Ossineke area fill out the list. U.S. 23 hugs the shoreline, M-32 ends in downtown Alpena, and M-65 offers a quicker way south.

The Census Bureau puts mid-2025 headcount at 28,853, down 0.2 percent from 2020, and seniors make up 27.9 percent. Four of every five homes are lived in by their owners. The typical household earns $53,950, workers spend 17.5 minutes getting to work, and gross rent has a median of $673. Employers in 2023 numbered 822, jobs 10,141, and shoppers spent roughly $616 million in 2022.

Assessments are a local matter, so a seller with a parcel question should call the city or township assessor, not the register.

sections.h2: How have Alpena County's population and housing changed over time?
sections.html:
Population topped out at 32,315 in 1980, then slid to 30,605 by 1990, 29,598 by 2010 and 28,907 by 2020.

The 2020 to 2024 Census data counts 13,019 households with 2.17 people each and 15,768 housing units as of 2025. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,096, and owners without one pay $455. Poverty affects 16.7 percent of residents, and 18.3 percent of adults 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree.

The land itself is part of the story. Glaciers left a Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine barrens and hardwood forest, and large inland lakes such as Long Lake and Grand Lake sit north of the city along U.S. 23.

sections.h2: What do the work and household numbers say about Alpena County?
sections.html:
Alpena County recorded 72 building permits in 2025, a small figure beside its 15,768 housing units. Census data shows 89.4 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier.

Some 53.7 percent of people 16 and older are in the civilian labor force. Employers number 822, with 817 firms counted in the 2023 reference year and a further 1,849 nonemployer businesses in 2024. Annual payroll for employer establishments came to about $476.6 million in 2023, and employment grew 3.4 percent between 2022 and 2023.

The county has 2,310 veterans, and 85.1 percent of households have a broadband subscription. The original residents of the area were the Thunder Bay Band of Chippewa and Ottawa, who later merged with the Mackinac Bands, and offshore islands in Thunder Bay belong to the Michigan Islands National Wildlife Refuge.

faqs.q: What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alpena County?
faqs.a: Paper filings are taken until 4:00 p.m. and e-recordings until 3:30 p.m. A deed that arrives later is recorded on the next business day.

faqs.q: How can I contact the Alpena County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Phone 989-354-9547 or fax 989-354-9646, or visit 720 W. Chisholm Street, Suite 4, in Alpena.

faqs.q: Will my original deed come back from the Alpena County register?
faqs.a: Yes. The office indexes the paper and then returns the original, usually within a week of the recording date.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to a $153,900 sale in Alpena County?
faqs.a: The total is $1,324.40, which splits into $1,155.00 for the state and $169.40 for the county. Each rate applies to every $500 or fraction thereof.

faqs.q: Can Alpena County staff write or advise on my deed?
faqs.a: No. They do not complete documents, give legal advice or provide blank deeds. A title company, an attorney or an office supply store can help instead.
